subject: math.PR
name: Planar self-avoiding walk scaling limit
statement: For a simply connected planar domain with two marked boundary points, consider lattice self-avoiding paths between those points weighted by μ^(−length), where μ is the lattice connective constant. As the mesh tends to zero, do the unparameterized paths converge to chordal SLE_(8/3)?
importance: A central universality prediction for polymers and conformally invariant random curves.
status_note: The existence and conformal invariance of the lattice scaling limit are open; identifying a limit under those assumptions is not an existence proof.

references.title: Slade: The Self-Avoiding Walk: A Brief Survey

subject: math.PR
name: Conformal invariance of square-lattice critical percolation
statement: For independent bond percolation on the square lattice at p=1/2, prove that crossing probabilities in scaled Jordan domains converge to Cardy’s conformally invariant formula, and that the associated exploration interfaces converge to SLE_6.
importance: Would establish the central planar-percolation universality prediction beyond the special solved lattice.
status_note: Critical site percolation on the triangular lattice is understood; that theorem does not cover square-lattice bond percolation.

references.title: Smirnov: Critical percolation in the plane: conformal invariance, Cardy’s formula, scaling limits

subject: math.PR
name: KPZ exponents for planar first-passage percolation
statement: For nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on Z² with independent exponential mean-one edge times, prove the predicted passage-time fluctuation exponent χ=1/3 and geodesic transversal-wandering exponent ξ=2/3, in a rigorous formulation of these scaling exponents.
importance: A flagship universality prediction for random growth and optimization in disordered media.
status_note: Exactly solvable directed last-passage models have these exponents; ordinary undirected first-passage percolation remains unresolved.

references.title: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation

subject: math.PR
name: Strict convexity of the first-passage limit shape
statement: For nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on Z² with independent exponential mean-one edge times, is its deterministic asymptotic limit shape strictly convex, so that its boundary contains no nontrivial line segment?
importance: A basic geometric question underlying the structure of random geodesics.
status_note: The shape theorem is proved; strict convexity does not follow from existence of a deterministic convex limit shape.

references.title: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation

subject: math.PR
name: Three-dimensional self-avoiding walk exponent
statement: For a uniformly chosen n-step nearest-neighbor self-avoiding walk on Z³ starting at the origin, prove that its mean squared endpoint distance is n^(2ν+o(1)), and determine the exponent ν.
importance: The basic size exponent of three-dimensional polymers is a major quantitative universality question.
status_note: Numerical estimates near ν=0.588 are not rigorous values; high-dimensional mean-field results do not determine the three-dimensional exponent.

references.title: Slade: The Self-Avoiding Walk: A Brief Survey

subject: math.PR
name: Three-dimensional Brownian intersection exponent
statement: Let two independent Brownian motions in R³ start at distinct fixed points of the unit sphere and each stop on first reaching the sphere of radius R. Determine the exponent ξ₃ governing the probability that their stopped paths are disjoint, R^(−ξ₃+o(1)), as R→∞.
importance: An exact exponent would explain fine geometry of three-dimensional random paths.
status_note: Existence and estimates for the exponent are known; the exact planar exponent does not determine its three-dimensional value.

references.title: An explicit lower bound for the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (2026)

subject: math.PR
name: Low-temperature spin-glass phase in three dimensions
statement: For the nearest-neighbor Edwards–Anderson Ising model on periodic boxes Λ_L in Z³ with independent centered Gaussian couplings and zero external field, prove that some finite inverse temperature β has liminf as L→∞ of E_J〈q_L²〉_(β,J)>0. Here q_L=|Λ_L|^(-1)∑_x σ_xτ_x is the overlap of two independent Gibbs configurations with the same couplings.
importance: A central probability question about ordering in finite-dimensional disordered systems.
status_note: Mean-field spin-glass theory and numerical evidence do not prove a spin-glass phase for the three-dimensional short-range model.

subject: math.PR
name: Temperature chaos in the pure SK model
statement: In the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with the same Gaussian couplings, sample independent configurations at distinct inverse temperatures β₁,β₂>1. Does their normalized spin overlap tend to 0 in probability under the joint Gibbs law as the number of spins tends to infinity?
importance: Tests whether a small temperature change reorganizes a disordered equilibrium state completely.
status_note: Temperature-chaos theorems for generic mixed-spin models do not settle the pure two-spin SK case.

references.title: Panchenko: Chaos in temperature in generic 2p-spin models

subject: math.PR
name: Two-dimensional Anderson localization at arbitrary disorder
statement: For Hψ(x)=∑_(|y−x|=1)ψ(y)+λV_xψ(x) on ℓ²(Z²), with independent V_x uniform on [−1,1], prove that for every λ>0 the spectrum is almost surely pure point with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.
importance: A fundamental probability problem about whether arbitrarily weak planar disorder prevents wave propagation.
status_note: Localization at strong disorder and near spectral edges is known; the full weak-disorder two-dimensional assertion remains open. Results on trees and hyperbolic lattices concern different geometry.

references.title: Becker and Oltman: Disorder on the hyperbolic square lattice I: Anderson delocalization and absolutely continuous spectrum (2026), introduction

subject: math.PR
name: Exact dimension of three-dimensional loop-erased walk
statement: Determine the exact growth exponent, equivalently the predicted fractal dimension, of the scaling limit of nearest-neighbor loop-erased random walk in R³. In the lattice formulation, ask for the exponent β₃ in the expected number of loop-erased steps before leaving a ball of radius R, R^(β₃+o(1)).
importance: A basic quantitative question about random paths and uniform spanning trees in three dimensions.
status_note: Scaling-limit and exponent-existence results do not give the exact three-dimensional exponent; the planar value 5/4 is not applicable.

references.title: An explicit lower bound for the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (2026)
